name: encoding-single
algorithm: windows-1252 to UTF-8 of a French line with curly quotes, a dash and a euro sign repeated n times, rounds times, by Mk's std decoder; the checksum adds per round the output length and one output byte at a moving index (README.md).

skip.c: no std single-byte decoder: C's standard library has none (iconv is POSIX, not ISO C); no library stands in
skip.rust: no std single-byte decoder: encoding_rs is a crate; no crate stands in
skip.zig: no std single-byte decoder: Zig's std.unicode has UTF-8 and UTF-16 only
skip.go: no std single-byte decoder: golang.org/x/text/encoding/charmap is not std; no module stands in
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, and this one has the Mk column only; the decoder is tested by the lane's Go tests (TestStdEncoding_SingleByteIndexRoundTrip, TestStdEncoding_DecodeAdversarial, TestStdEncoding_LongInputs)
notes: An Mk-only throughput row: no standard library among C, Rust, Zig and Go has a legacy single-byte decoder (skip), so there is no ratio. Until the std-encoding fix round (2026-11-12) the row held hand-written table loops in C, Rust and Go; plan/06-m6.md section 4.1 keeps the two tables apart and fills a cell with no standard facility with its reason, so they were removed.
Mk: encoding.Windows1252.Decode into an arena reset each round (sized in one pass, written in a second: Mk's API).

Checksums: Go's at both sizes on the owner's machine (std-encoding session 2, 2026-11-12, from the former Go column, which wrote what the WHATWG decoder writes); tools/bench checks the Mk column against them.
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
